descriptions.text:
Hindi 1 is an introductory course designed for students with no prior knowledge or only minimal exposure to Hindi. Hindi, an Indo-European language, is the third most widely spoken language in the world and serves as one of the official languages of the Indian Union. Proficiency in Hindi opens doors to a vast and diverse cultural and economic landscape, spanning literature, cinema, music, and one of the world’s largest markets.

This course introduces the Hindustani variety of Hindi, the lingua franca of much of the Indian subcontinent, and aims to develop elementary proficiency by building students’ listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. As part of this, students will gain an awareness of the close relationship between Hindi and Urdu, which share a common linguistic base but differ in script, register, and cultural context. Learners will also be introduced to the Devanagari script, which is used to write Hindi.

Focusing on all four language skills and the three modes of communication—interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational—the course blends a communicative approach with a range of engaging methods. In-class activities, formative assessments, video clips, authentic materials, and interactive tasks supplement core course content. To support vocabulary and grammar development, the course incorporates audio-visual resources, including popular Bollywood songs.

Following a blended learning model, the course combines in-person instruction with the thoughtful integration of online tools for both classroom and independent learning. A selection of the methods and tools used in this course, along with examples of student work, can be explored **[here](https://tandemhindi.wordpress.com/)**.

* Rupert Snell; _Get Started in Hindi_ [With audio CD]; London: Hodder; 2014 [ISBN-13: 9781444174687]* Rupert Snell; _Essential Hindi Dictionary: A Teach Yourself Guide_; London: Hodder; 2011 [ISBN-13: 9781444104004]

* Written & Oral exams and quizzes
* Individual or group Project work
* In-class oral / listening performance & home assignments

### Weighing

Reading: 20%
Writing: 20%
Listening: 20%
Speaking: 20%
Participation & Homework Assignments: 20%

There will be no make-ups for any missed quiz; presentation or other assessment activity. Only in case of a medical or personal emergency should the lecturer be informed immediately by e-mail with documented evidence for special consideration.

By the end of the course; students should have reached approximately the A1 standard of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR). This course is the first course in a series of four language acquisition courses within the BA South & South-East Asian Studies.

The main objectives of the course are:

* Elementary knowledge of vocabulary and sentence structures of Hindi to a simple level to listen; speak; read; and write simple spoken language in practical day to day situations.
* Elementary knowledge of the grammar of Hindi and the ability to apply this knowledge in their own oral and written language.
* Ability to read and write simple words and sentences in Devanagari script of Hindi.
* Be familiar with related cultural information about India / South Asia; e.g. greetings; clothes; food; society; social etiquettes etc.

CEFR Level:
Reading - A1
Writing - A1 
Listening - A1 
Speaking - A1

* For substantive questions; contact the lecturer listed in the right information bar.* For questions about enrolment; admission; etc; contact the Education Administration Office [Herta Mohr](https://www.organisatiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/en/faculties-and-institutes/humanities/faculty-office/student-affairs/education-administration-offices/herta-mohr-education-administration-office)

This course adopts an integrated, communicative approach to language learning, emphasizing interaction and meaningful language use. Active participation in classroom activities is essential for achieving the intended learning outcomes

* Seminar (three two hour tutorials every week)Attendance and participation are obligatory. Classes missed for a good reason (to the discretion of the conveners and to be discussed BEFORE the class takes place) will have to be made up with an extra assignment. Being absent without notification can result in a lower grade or exclusion from the term end exams and a failing grade for the course.Being absent will result in a lowering of the In-class performance & participation grade with 0.5 for every absence after the first five (5) times.

#### Resit

If the end grade is insufficient, there is a possibility of retaking only the term end written exam in the course (25%). Individual exams cannot be retaken.

The course is an integrated whole. The final examination and the assignments must be completed in the same academic year. No partial marks can be carried over into following years.

#### Review and feedback

How and when an exam review will take place will be disclosed together with the publication of the exam results at the latest. If a student requests a review within 30 days after publication of the exam results, an exam review will have to be organized.

descriptions.value: Analysing situations or information and deciding what is of major and lesser importance. Seeing interrelationships and getting to the core of the matter.
Ontleden van situaties of een hoeveelheid informatie in hoofd- en bijzaken. Zien van onderlinge verbanden en doordringen tot de kern.
Achieving a result by effectively and systematically utilising and overseeing activities, time and resources.
Een resultaat bereiken door het effectief en planmatig inzetten en overzien van activiteiten, tijd en middelen.
Contributing to a joint result with other people or groups, even when this is not in your own personal interest.
Bijdragen aan een gezamenlijk resultaat met andere personen of groepen, ook wanneer dit niet van direct persoonlijk belang is.
Making ideas and information clear to others through spoken words, using comprehensible language and checking that the message has been understood.
Ideeën en informatie in begrijpelijke gesproken taal aan anderen duidelijk maken en nagaan of de boodschap begrepen is.
Setting out ideas and information clearly in writing, taking account of the relevant target group and in such a way that the message is received and understood.
Ideeën en informatie helder op schrift stellen, rekening houdend met de doelgroep, en zodanig dat de boodschap overkomt en wordt begrepen.
Conveying ideas and information clearly to an audience, taking account of the target group and using appropriate supporting materials and platforms.
Ideeën en informatie op heldere wijze overbrengen aan een publiek, rekening houdend met de doelgroep. Hierbij worden passende ondersteunende materialen en platformen gebruikt.
Being well-informed about societal, political and discipline-related developments and being aware of own role and influence within these developments.
Goed geïnformeerd zijn over de maatschappelijke, politieke en vakinhoudelijke ontwikkelingen en zich bewust zijn van de eigen rol en invloed binnen deze ontwikkelingen.

Critically evaluating own and others’ behaviour, viewpoints or methods, and being open to evaluation by others. Being able to learn from these evaluations by changing own behaviour, viewpoints or methods.

Het kritisch evalueren van (eigen) gedrag, standpunten of methoden en open staan voor evaluatie door anderen. Het vermogen om te leren van deze evaluaties door wijziging van het eigen gedrag, standpunten of methoden.
Self-directing own process of absorbing and applying new knowledge and information.
Zelf sturing geven aan het eigen proces van nieuwe kennis en informatie opnemen en toepassen.
